trigger: the replay guard is set below about 10 s, or at default config a verdict replay is followed by a breaker-recovery full replay of a session the server already knows
classification_rationale: a required statement is missing from the manual and the ADR; the omission conceals security-relevant behaviour, which raises I7 from MEDIUM to HIGH
summary: gateway.md and the ADR never said that replaying a session the server already knows has side effects: the server re-adopts it, revokes the agent's device tokens (dormant today) and installs a fresh session so placement is lost until the reannounce lands. Documented in b4c603ac4 and mirrored in the ADR in 7d140dfde. The optional floor on the guard was not adopted (range still 0 to 3600000).

trigger: a compromised server or a plaintext gateway-server link returns a reject_reason carrying CR, LF or ESC
classification_rationale: the reject_reason was logged with ~s after a 128 byte cut but control bytes passed through into a log line
summary: Bytes below 32 and DEL are replaced by a question mark per byte after the cut, b8621ac9f. The C1 range 0x80 to 0x9F was found in the re-review as G8-c1-control-bytes.

trigger: any verdict with two or more ids
classification_rationale: the buffer sorts a verdict's ids, so the replay queue is in session id order, not the order the server listed; docs and comments said otherwise. Also reported by happy-path. The accepted-default comment in do_replay_one was reported in the same finding
summary: Comments corrected in a1ff791db (queue order, accepted default); gateway.md wording corrected in b4c603ac4.

trigger: the server sets the truncated flag on every response of a long recovery (more than 4096 unknown sessions from one gateway in one batch)
classification_rationale: a WARN is emitted on every flush while the server-controlled flag is set, about once per second at the default interval; no rate limit
summary: Not changed in either fix round; gateway.md documents the WARN and calls it informational. Owner decides whether to rate limit it; no issue filed.

trigger: a BatchHeartbeat OK answer with trailers and no DATA frame, which grpcbox returns as {ok, <<>>, Trailers}
classification_rationale: consume_verdict called maps:get on a non-map body and raised badmap, killing the buffer process and its buffered heartbeats; reproduced with a mocked grpcbox_client
summary: A non-map body is no verdict and a non-list unknown_session_ids is treated as absent, 4b4b7a653. The same shape in the replay path and in the agent service was found in the re-review as G8-up-2.

trigger: any crash of the upstream process while the replay queue holds RegisterRequests (enrollment_token, machine_certificate, csr_pem)
classification_rationale: the stored requests were printed whole in a crash report: credentials in the log, and 28 s and 179 MB of log for 10000 entries (measured). The reporter left I1 for the security-guardian to adjudicate; the security-guardian derived HIGH for the same class in the re-review (G8-sg-1), so I1 is recorded here and the band derives HIGH. The reporter's own label was MEDIUM
summary: format_status/1 now reports scalar fields with the queue and the stamp map reduced to sizes, and the last message without the request, 6322c7a18. The remaining unredacted crash report paths were found in the re-review as G8-sg-1.

trigger: a direct call to the exported replay_sessions/1 with a very large id list (100k ids took 20 ms to 601 ms and up to 27 MB; only the buffer calls it and it caps at 4096)
classification_rationale: the exported function had no cap or type check at the cast boundary; the reporter derived I9 with E6, recorded here as I8 with E5 because E6 (outcome proven unable to occur) is not established for a direct call
summary: The cast handler ignores a non-list and cuts a list to the same 4096 bound before counting, dropping or queueing, a663de788.

trigger: a verdict cast rate above about 35 to 40 per second, for example heartbeat_batch_interval_ms set far below the 1000 ms default (the key has no validation)
classification_rationale: measured at 100 casts per second: the upstream mailbox peaked at 116 messages and 92 MB in 6 s and the drip was starved (17 RPCs against about 220 unloaded); no growth at 10 per second. Derived MEDIUM, the reporter's label was NICE
summary: Not changed in either fix round (no drop-if-busy check in the buffer, no validation of the interval key). Needs an owner decision: guard the buffer, validate the key, or document the limit.

trigger: registration_replay_spacing_ms set to -5, foo or 1.5 in sys.config
classification_rationale: an invalid value crashes the upstream process at its first pop (badarg in send_after); the architect also reported the key as unvalidated while the two new keys go through env_int. A non-default invalid configuration that crashes the process derives MEDIUM, the reporter's label was NICE
summary: Not changed in either fix round. The key is pre-existing and unvalidated; validating it like the two new keys is a small follow-up for the owner.

trigger: the server's ProxyRegister fails (INTERNAL or UNAVAILABLE) while a verdict drip runs, including the directory-unavailable case
classification_rationale: replay failures reach the shared circuit breaker (and through it the /readyz answer) but the manual said only that the breaker policy is unchanged
summary: Section 'Replay failures feed the shared circuit breaker' added in b4c603ac4; the whole-readyz consequence of an open breaker added in fd90a5bc4.

trigger: the server keeps listing a session after it was replayed
classification_rationale: the runbook said that all three counters staying at 0 means no verdict reaches the replay, but ids already queued or inside the guard window are deliberately uncounted, so a non-converging case also leaves them at 0. Reporter label was SHOULD, derived LOW
summary: The inference sentence was replaced by per-counter guidance in b4c603ac4 and qualified further in 6f11ea615.

trigger: an operator alerts on a persistently non-zero yuzu_gw_registration_replay_queue_depth as the manual advises
classification_rationale: the manual says a persistently non-zero queue depth means a replay that never drains and to alert on it, while its own load table makes a non-zero depth normal for 250 to 1200 s at 10k agents
summary: The metric row in gateway.md still carries the sentence at the branch tip. Add a duration qualifier or drop the sentence; no alert rule ships.

trigger: the breaker is half open or closed with prior failures while a verdict names at least one session, and other agents the server still holds need a full re-proxy (for example tombstoned route rows after a long outage)
classification_rationale: a breaker-recovery full replay is dropped while a targeted queue runs, and a drip RPC that closes the breaker discards the replay signal, so the docs saying the breaker policy is unchanged and that trigger=breaker replays every agent were wrong. Also reported by gateway-erlang. Reporter label was SHOULD, derived LOW
summary: Wording corrected in b4c603ac4 (a breaker recovery trigger is dropped while a verdict drip is queued; stated as a limit). The behaviour is unchanged: the full replay can still be swallowed in the two arms. Owner files an issue; none exists yet.

trigger: the server stays up while an agent's route row is tombstoned (an outage of about 270 s or more), so nothing lists the session in a verdict
classification_rationale: no open issue covers the route row tombstoned while the server stays up; the ADR relates it to a different mechanism (the reaper versus drip race)
summary: Documented as a known limit. Owner files an issue; none exists yet. Suggested order from the review: the idempotent same-session adopt first, then a server-side extension of the verdict to name sessions with a renew shortfall.

trigger: an operator or reviewer follows the docs' follow-up wording to find the tracking issues
classification_rationale: the docs said follow-up with no issue numbers although the idempotent adopt, the in-flight notification limit, the verdict follow-ups and the disconnect-without-guard issues exist. Also reported by compliance-officer and consistency-auditor
summary: The related issues are cited in the manual and the evidence record: b4c603ac4, 6d3e3dbf6.

trigger: a reader relies on the ADR multi-replica paragraph to understand what a same-session re-adopt does
classification_rationale: the paragraph omitted the device-token revoke a same-session re-adopt triggers, which gateway.proto already states and which the security-guardian rated HIGH in the manual (sg-F1). Recorded as I7 (MEDIUM) for the ADR; the reporter's label was NICE
summary: The ADR now states the device-token revoke and the placement loss, b4c603ac4.

trigger: a reader takes the ADR wording at face value
classification_rationale: three smaller inexact statements in the same finding: 'rising at the guard rate' (verdict ids come only from heartbeating sessions about 30 s apart), the session index described as written only by register_agent/7 and the fenced deregister (deletes also occur elsewhere), and rig numbers duplicated in the ADR and the manual
summary: Not changed in either fix round (the guard rate sentence and the writer enumeration are still in the ADR at the branch tip).

trigger: an operator reads the queue cap key description
classification_rationale: registration_replay_queue_max bounds only verdict appends; the breaker-seeded snapshot is uncapped (bounded by the local agent count) and the docs and the moduledoc said the cap bounds the queue
summary: Queue and cap wording corrected in b4c603ac4.

trigger: new yuzu_gw_upstream code is hot loaded into a running node
classification_rationale: the state record gained fields and code_change/3 is the identity, so a hot load fails on the next message and the supervisor restarts the process; the reporter said no hot-upgrade path is documented
summary: Informational. The manual already says at the reviewed sha 'Restart the gateway to deploy this behaviour' (gateway.md line 786) and describes the hot-load behaviour; no change made. Recorded by the ledger writer from the reviewed sha and the branch tip, not adjudicated by the reporter.

trigger: an operator reads the yuzu_server_gateway_route_desync_total row after upgrading both server and gateway
classification_rationale: the row still called a sustained unknown_session rise a known limitation under Server-Side Setup (a note this change deleted) and said only a full restart recovered it. Also reported by enterprise-readiness and consistency-auditor
summary: Row rewritten to point at the reconcile runbook, b4c603ac4.

trigger: a reader follows the WS-4 row's pointer to the known limitation under Server-Side Setup
classification_rationale: the pointer resolves to a section that no longer holds the note. Also reported by consistency-auditor
summary: Pointer replaced in b4c603ac4; the unrelated rewording of the row found by compliance-officer was reverted in 9b31db415.

trigger: a reader takes 'largest real run was 27 agents' as a replay measurement
classification_rationale: the figure comes from the heartbeat connection-binding soak, which did not exercise the drip, while the same section says more than one agent was not tested
summary: The source run is named and the sentence says it did not exercise the replay drip, b4c603ac4.

trigger: a reader reads 'registers directly' as the non-gateway server path
classification_rationale: the phrase also appears in the ADR; it reads as a direct-to-server registration rather than a re-registration through the gateway
summary: Wording changed in b4c603ac4 (no occurrence remains at the branch tip).

trigger: an operator reads the HELP text of yuzu_gw_registration_replay_total
classification_rationale: HELP said total agents re-proxied but the counter increments on every drip attempt (success, failure, accepted=false, superseded), as the manual and the Grafana README state. Also reported by consistency-auditor
summary: HELP text and handler comment corrected, 56f07cb8c.

trigger: an operator reads the changelog bound for recovery while the breaker is open
classification_rationale: the fragment said at most 300 s once the backoff ends; the manual, the ADR and the upgrade note add the heartbeat interval, the flush and the drip position, and the unqualified advice to use --no-auto-update disables the OTA patch channel. Also reported by compliance-officer and enterprise-readiness
summary: Bound stated honestly and the --no-auto-update advice qualified, 388415376.

trigger: the release notes are assembled with both the earlier and the new fragment
classification_rationale: the earlier fragment's headline still read inert, does not fix #1197, next to the new Fixed entry. Also reported by docs-writer and compliance-officer
summary: Headline reworded so the assembled notes read coherently, 388415376.

trigger: an operator sees the registry-unavailable abort WARN, or reads about the accepted=false disconnect
classification_rationale: the new WARN 'Registration replay aborted: registry unavailable' was not in the runbook, and the new disconnect site inherits the missing session-match guard tracked in #4629 with no cross-reference
summary: Log lines and the #4629 cross-reference added in b4c603ac4; the abort wording corrected in fd90a5bc4 and f4b61e372.

trigger: removing prune_recent_replays at the circuit-open abort or the registry-unavailable abort
classification_rationale: mutants survived on both abort arms because both tests run under the 10000 ms guard where the stamp is fresh
summary: Stamp prune pinned on both abort arms with a short guard fixture, df3f09045.

trigger: deleting the emit_queue_depth call in the pop-time skip clause
classification_rationale: the mutant survived: the re-registered agent test never asserted the depth report
summary: The queue depth report at the pop-time skip is asserted, df3f09045.

trigger: running the registration replay test module
classification_rationale: bind_agent/2 left about 60 idle dummy processes in the VM; older tests killed theirs. Test-only, no cross-test effect
summary: The dummy processes are killed at cleanup, df3f09045.

trigger: an auditor or reviewer looks for the rig evidence behind the manual's observed figures
classification_rationale: the rig timings cited by the manual and the ADR were not in a retrievable record (CC8.1); the docs labelled them local-only. The reporter derived I9, label SHOULD
summary: Evidence record committed under docs/security-reviews, 6d3e3dbf6, and corrected in the re-review round (see G8-evidence-record-misstated).

trigger: a reviewer reads the earlier ledger fragment for the server-side verdict change
classification_rationale: two rows are still deferred-to-issue #?, the truncation counter row is still linked-to-#1197 although the counter is now delivered, and the six-obligation row can carry only one disposition
summary: The six-obligation row is answered by the F-prc-obligations row in this fragment. The earlier fragment is not edited from this branch, so the F-test-concurrency and F-desync-seam rows (still deferred-to-issue #?) and the F-trunc-counter row (delivered in 820513981 and 908510c46) need superseding rows from their owner.

trigger: a reader sees an internal change label in comments, the ADR heading or the HA matrix
classification_rationale: the diff added 21 lines carrying an internal change label that an earlier finding had already removed from the neighbouring work
summary: Removed from the ADR and the matrix in b4c603ac4 and 9b31db415, and from the code comments in 5c42941f6.

trigger: a reviewer reads the WS-4 row diff and the observability conventions diff
classification_rationale: about 80 dash substitutions and two reworded security phrases in lines this change did not own, undisclosed in the commit messages, hid the real addition. Also reported by consistency-auditor and enterprise-readiness
summary: Both files restored from the merge base and the intended additions re-applied as minimal insertions, 9b31db415.

trigger: an operator sees a notify_dropped rise, the R2b limit, the open-breaker drop or an accepted=false answer
classification_rationale: four gaps between signal and action: no action for notify_dropped, no recovery statement for the R2b limit, the breaker-open log lines missing from the what-you-should-see table, and accepted=false described as admin-denied only
summary: Operator actions, log lines and the accepted=false causes added in b4c603ac4; per-reason actions qualified in 6f11ea615.

trigger: the server is upgraded first, so the restart that ships this fix meets the old gateway and agents read offline
classification_rationale: the note implied that an upgraded gateway recovers the window but gave no stated action or tested status; a gateway restart also drops every agent stream
summary: The upgrade-day window and its action are stated in b4c603ac4 and were corrected further in the re-review (G8-sre-1, fd90a5bc4).

trigger: a mass FAILED_PRECONDITION or accepted=false answer, for example after a Postgres restore to an older snapshot before a server restart
classification_rationale: the replay disconnects the agent on accepted=false or FAILED_PRECONDITION; per the OTA wedge (#2182) released default agents then stay dark for up to 6 h. Derived MEDIUM in the reporter's register (reasoned from the server code, not run)
summary: Behaviour unchanged by design; the interim operator action is documented (b4c603ac4, fd90a5bc4). Not adjudicated as accepted. Owner decides whether it needs a follow-up issue.

trigger: an adopt succeeds and the following dispatch notify is dropped (circuit_open or at_capacity)
classification_rationale: the agent is acknowledged by the server but undispatchable until it reconnects; derived MEDIUM in the reporter's register and HIGH only if adjudicated as a wedged state machine (I5 case c)
summary: Declared as a known follow-up in the docs, which cite #4632 (in-flight notification limit) and #5244 (idempotent adopt) as related. No issue filed for the gap itself.

trigger: a crash of the upstream process while registrations are in flight
classification_rationale: format_status redacted the queue and the last message but the crash report still printed the exit reason, the stacktrace argument lists, the sys log, and the process mailbox and proc_lib messages and exception lines, which carry in-flight registrations (credentials). Verified on a stand-in probe. Also reported independently by gateway-erlang (G8-erl-1) and unhappy-path (G8-up-1). Reporter label MEDIUM, derived HIGH
summary: Fixed in part: exit reason and sys log redaction, stacktrace frames keep arity, file and line only, and the RPC body exception is caught so a request no longer reaches a crash report through the stacktrace (576ebf338). Reason redaction is defensive only because OTP appends the stacktrace after format_status; the RPC wrap closes the RPC exception route. The mailbox and proc_lib routes are recorded separately as G8-sg-1-residual-mailbox.

trigger: a crash of the upstream process with registrations in its mailbox or in a proc_lib crash report
classification_rationale: the mailbox and the proc_lib messages and exception lines of a crash report are printed from raw data and cannot be closed from format_status
summary: Disclosed in the gateway manual Known limits, the ADR note and the evidence record (6f11ea615 to f4b61e372), and the unredacted routes are listed under Not tested in the evidence record. The author treats the residual as accepted; no independent adjudicator has accepted a derived-HIGH residual, so it is recorded open and is not released by this row.

trigger: an operator follows the upgrade-day guidance, upgrades the server first and restarts the gateway with released v0.13.0 or rc6 agents connected
classification_rationale: the guidance omitted that a gateway restart disconnects every agent the node holds and that released agents can stay wedged until their service is restarted, which is harmful operator guidance that conceals the real state
summary: Upgrade-day advice now states the disconnect and that released agents may need an agent service restart, fd90a5bc4; mirrored in the ADR, conventions and changelog, 7d140dfde.

trigger: the circuit breaker is open while a load balancer probes :8081/readyz
classification_rationale: an open breaker makes the whole /readyz answer 503, which can take the node out of rotation; undocumented, with no escalation signal
summary: Stated in the runbook with the half-open probe-failed row and the breaker tuning keys, fd90a5bc4.

trigger: the registry process restarts mid replay and the abort WARN fires
classification_rationale: the registry-unavailable row claimed agents are listed again by a later verdict, and the code WARN said they return on their next heartbeat; both are wrong because the tables were lost and the verdict finds no local session (counted not_local)
summary: Runbook row corrected in fd90a5bc4; the WARN text reworded in f4b61e372.

trigger: an OK answer from the upstream with trailers and no DATA frame
classification_rationale: do_replay_one's {ok, Response} arm and yuzu_gw_agent_service:register raised badmap on a non-map OK body, killing the drip, the queue and the breaker state; the first fix round had closed only the buffer path (uph-1). Mutant check verified
summary: A non-map OK is a replay failure counted by the breaker, one warning naming neither the session id nor the body, and the register path answers INTERNAL, 0571020dd; the proxy_register ok payload spec widened, 81aa38ebf.

trigger: a reviewer relies on the evidence record for what was rig-tested and what the earlier ledger obligations decided
classification_rationale: the record listed code changes made after the rig run as tests or comments only, presented the declined obligations as recorded fact though the reasons were reconstructed, listed 3 of 6 obligations and overstated 'met', and pointed at a ledger fragment that did not exist yet. Also reported by enterprise-readiness, compliance-officer and consistency-auditor (the pairing of those three reviewers to individual ids was not recorded)
summary: The rig-tested commit is separated from later code commits, all six obligations are listed with a status and the reasons marked reconstructed, 3b74b86d9 and f4b61e372. The ledger pointer resolves once this fragment is committed.

trigger: the server stays up while an agent's route row is tombstoned, and the breaker-recovery repair is lost
classification_rationale: the route row tombstoned while the server stays up has no issue; the docs say it is tracked as a follow-up
summary: Owner files an issue. Same gap as arch-F2-r2b-tombstone-gap-no-issue from the first review.

trigger: the server returns text with bytes 0x80 to 0x9F, which ~s renders as Latin-1 code points (U+0085 NEL, U+009B CSI)
classification_rationale: reject_reason_for_log replaced C0 and DEL but let the C1 range through, and the failed-RPC warning logged the server's grpc-message unsanitised (a sibling site outside the diff)
summary: C1 bytes are replaced after the 128 byte cut and the failed-RPC warning goes through the same sanitiser, 87f48a559.

trigger: a queue or stamp field of the wrong type reaches format_status
classification_rationale: redact_state was not total; reported at INFO by a Gate 8 reviewer (which one was not recorded)
summary: redact_state is total: a field of the wrong type shows as '$redacted', 576ebf338.

trigger: an operator reads the HELP of yuzu_gw_heartbeat_unknown_truncated_total
classification_rationale: HELP said omitted sessions are reported again by later heartbeats, which gateway.proto does not guarantee; reported by a Gate 8 reviewer (which one was not recorded)
summary: HELP now says may be reported again, 8c9a4d26d.

trigger: a reader sees the internal change label in about 20 code comments, or the test variable named Hostile
classification_rationale: an internal change label recurred in comments and a test variable name was loaded; reported by Gate 8 reviewers (which one was not recorded)
summary: Label reworded to the issue number or plain wording at about 20 sites, the variable renamed Crafted, and the accepted=false comment rewrapped; comments only, 5c42941f6.

trigger: an operator reads the runbook for the not_local, queue_full, malformed and truncated outcomes
classification_rationale: grouped NICE items from sre, enterprise-readiness, docs-writer, compliance-officer and consistency-auditor: missing operator actions per outcome, unmarked derived claims, the 270 versus 300 s reap horizon wording, the guard floor and sizing wording, and the earlier fragment filename pointer. The pairing of reviewers to individual ids was not recorded
summary: Qualified and reworded across fd90a5bc4, 7d140dfde, 6f11ea615 and f4b61e372.

trigger: the gateway-side replay acting on a stale, disconnected or flood-influenced verdict (the six obligations the server-side verdict change recorded for the gateway consumer)
classification_rationale: this row supersedes, in this fragment only, the F-prc-obligations row of governance.d/1197-batch-heartbeat-unknown-sessions.1sz0KG.jsonl (disposition linked-to-#1197, no rationale), which is not edited. The reasons below were reconstructed from the code at the branch tip and are not a recovered decision
summary: Status per obligation, exactly as in docs/security-reviews/gateway-heartbeat-verdict-replay-2026-10-04.md: (1) replay only ids seen in two batches: not adopted, reason reconstructed (liveness is re-checked at queue time and before every send, a per-agent pending entry and the guard window bound repeats, a second batch only adds up to one heartbeat interval of latency); (2) liveness at replay time: met by entries_for_sessions/1 at queue time and lookup_local_session/1 before each send; (3) dedupe against the queue and reuse the drip pacing: met by one pending entry per agent, the per-session guard window and the existing drip spacing; (4) suppress while the directory is unavailable and exclude from breaker accounting: two halves, suppression is approximated not met (a verdict while the breaker is open is dropped, one arriving half open is queued on purpose because its first replay is the probe), and excluding replays from breaker accounting is not adopted, reason reconstructed (a replay answered UNAVAILABLE must still count so a failing server can open the breaker); (5) a verdict-ever-seen gauge for version skew: not adopted, reason reconstructed (skew is a no-op in both directions, and replay_triggered_total{trigger=heartbeat} and replay_total show whether replays are sent); (6) sanitise ids before logging: met for the ids the server lists (counts only), while the pre-existing DEBUG line that logs the session id the server returned is unsanitised and was not touched (inferred from the code). The disposition fixed records that the obligations were addressed; three are met in code and the declined parts carry reconstructed reasons, not a recovered decision.

trigger: the upstream or registry process is absent, stalls past 30 s or dies while proxy_register, proxy_inventory or register_agent is in a bare gen_server:call
classification_rationale: the caller-side exit reason embedded the whole RegisterRequest (enrollment token, csr_pem, machine certificate) and reached the grpcbox crash log, which the crash report filter never sees; the same bare call exists on origin/dev. Reported independently by gateway-erlang and security-guardian
summary: Fixed in ca614c5c1: yuzu_gw_safe_call turns every such exit into an error atom and never keeps the reason; a WARN names only the class of the exit, at most once per second per server. Tests run each call uncaught and under the grpcbox catch-and-log with the filter installed, with a raw-call control. Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: a yuzu_gw_agent process crashes, or a call it makes fails, while it holds register_req in its data record
classification_rationale: the agent held the verbatim RegisterRequest with no format_status, so the gen_statem terminate report, the proc_lib crash report and the supervisor report printed the enrollment token, certificate and CSR
summary: Fixed in 84a5ca0a2 (format_status for the agent and registry processes, filter coverage widened to match them by name, by init/1 and by supervisor child spec) and 848709698 (dialyzer-clean map form). Real agent and registry processes crash in the tests with the filter, with format_status alone and with neither as a control. Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: an operator reads the HELP text of the verdict-dropped counter after the queue_full reason was widened to cover the upstream mailbox bound
classification_rationale: queue_full counts ids dropped at the replay queue cap and also ids not cast because the upstream mailbox held more than 100 messages; the HELP and comments named only the first, which points an operator at the wrong queue. Reported at MEDIUM
summary: Fixed in 63853a007: the HELP text and comments state both causes.

trigger: a node is hot upgraded with the shipped appup while the upstream state record has gained fields and code_change/3 is the identity
classification_rationale: the appup/relup are stale against the new state records. Reported at MEDIUM with low confidence. Adjudicated by the owner session: hot code upgrade is unsupported (no relup exists anywhere in the gateway and the manual says to restart the gateway to deploy), so the reported path is not a supported one. Recorded as rejected, the same way the earlier erl-F3-hot-load-needs-restart row was
summary: Not changed. The unsupported hot upgrade is now stated explicitly in the gateway manual and the ADR note (6f75c80a4). The rationale is that the deployment contract is restart, not that the stale files are correct. Same disposition as the earlier erl-F3 row.

trigger: a maintainer reads the helper duplication, the unbounded test wait, the test name and the WARN scope wording
classification_rationale: grouped NICE items of the first Gate 8 re-review: env_int duplicated between upstream and buffer, wait_until unbounded, a test name that overclaimed what it covers, and the per-process scope of the truncated WARN rate limit. The pairing of reviewers to individual items was not recorded
summary: Fixed in ced871824 (one shared bounded env_int in yuzu_gw_env), fda45ea70 (wait_until takes a name and a 3 s deadline; the test is renamed for what it covers) and 6f75c80a4 (WARN scope wording; nearest commit for that item).

trigger: one heartbeat whose status tags alone exceed the server's 4194304 byte receive limit (grpcbox applies no inbound cap)
classification_rationale: the heartbeat went out as a chunk of its own, was refused every cycle and held every newer heartbeat behind it, so a state machine wedged (I5 case c). Raised independently by gateway-erlang (HB-1), security-guardian (SG-3) and unhappy-path (F1)
summary: Fixed in e5cb45a70 (screen each heartbeat on arrival: over 512 tags or still over one chunk without its snapshot is dropped as heartbeat_oversize), 764490c80 (the heartbeat_oversize, heartbeat_invalid and chunk_rejected drop reasons), f3ddaf87e (a chunk the server refuses with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED or INVALID_ARGUMENT is dropped or split and the flush goes on) and 6b2885f2a (at most 8 chunks per flush). Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: a session id or status tag key or value that is not valid UTF-8, so gateway_pb:encode_msg raises badarg inside the flush
classification_rationale: the buffer process crashed and lost every buffered heartbeat. The reviewer derived CRITICAL; the recorded facts derive HIGH, the same BLOCKING band. The encoder path pre-dates the buffer rewrite
summary: Fixed in e5cb45a70 (a session id or tag that is not valid UTF-8 is dropped as heartbeat_invalid at arrival, the older entry is kept) and f3ddaf87e (an exception out of the RPC is caught, only its class is logged, and the entries the encoder raises on alone are dropped). Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: Register while the registry process is down: store_pending/2 makes a bare ets:insert into a table the registry owns
classification_rationale: the badarg stacktrace carried the RegisterRequest (enrollment token, certificate, CSR) into the grpcbox handler crash log; the bare insert exists on origin/dev
summary: Fixed in f292be52f: store_pending/2 and take_pending/1 catch badarg and return the fixed registry_unavailable error; the handler answers INTERNAL with a fixed message. Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: Subscribe while the agent supervisor is down: supervisor:start_child exits inside the handler with the request in its arguments
classification_rationale: the exit carried the RegisterRequest into the handler crash log; the call exists on origin/dev
summary: Fixed in f292be52f: start_agent/1 catches the exit through yuzu_gw_safe_call:guard/3 and returns agent_sup_unavailable; the handler logs a fixed line. Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: SendCommand while yuzu_gw_router is not running: a bare gen_server:call carrying the CommandRequest exits the management handler
classification_rationale: found by the implementing agent's own sweep of handler-process calls that carry a request, after the Register and Subscribe cases; the exit reason embeds the CommandRequest, whose plugin parameters may be secrets. The call exists on origin/dev. Reasoned from code, not run
summary: Fixed in 5114059fd: the call goes through yuzu_gw_safe_call and returns router_unavailable, which the handler already answers as a failed fanout.

trigger: an exit out of the HTTP/2 connection kills the heartbeat buffer (4 times in 150 s) while it holds fleet snapshots and tags
classification_rationale: OTP printed the whole 2 MB buffer state per report and the log grew to 173 MB; an escaped grpcbox exit also killed the buffer
summary: Fixed in f3ddaf87e (try/catch around the RPC) and 8016dd6a1 (format_status shows sizes and counts only, last message reduced to its tag, reason loses argument lists). Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: a backlog of many chunks is drained in one flush while casts queue in the buffer mailbox
classification_rationale: the buffer process was blocked for the whole backlog and the mailbox grew beyond the buffer caps meanwhile
summary: Fixed in 6b2885f2a: the timer flush and flush_sync/0 send at most 8 chunks (about 24 MiB) per cycle; the rest stays buffered.

trigger: a flush releases more than 8 MiB of binaries while the callback frame still holds the old state
classification_rationale: the explicit erlang:garbage_collect/0 did nothing (21.5 MB of released binaries stayed until an external GC) and two comments described the old behaviour
summary: Fixed in 095ba0352: the flush reports a release over 8 MiB and the callback returns continue; handle_continue/2 collects once the old state is unreferenced.

trigger: a flush larger than the synchronous call timeout, a first burst of safe-call failures, or an unbounded upstream_call_timeout_ms
classification_rationale: grouped LOW and INFO items: flush_sync cannot finish a 64 MiB drain though its doc said it blocks until done (F3), the safe-call WARN rate limit let the first concurrent burst each log (F4), and upstream_call_timeout_ms accepted any positive integer (INFO)
summary: Fixed in 6b2885f2a and 609888667 (F3: bounded flush plus doc), c92f670e8 (F4 and INFO: the WARN stamps are created once at application start; upstream_call_timeout_ms is read through env_int with range 100..300000).

trigger: an agent whose heartbeat carries an invalid UTF-8 or oversize status tag on every heartbeat
classification_rationale: the screen dropped the whole heartbeat, so a session sending bad tags every time never renewed the server's 90 s route lease or its telemetry (a wedged state machine, I5 case c). Reviewer derived HIGH
summary: Fixed in 2f5cfbb58: an invalid tag is repaired (each invalid byte becomes U+FFFD, counted heartbeat_invalid) and the heartbeat is kept; more than 512 tags or tags over a chunk drop only the tags (heartbeat_oversize).

trigger: a SendCommand with a negative timeout_seconds and one connected target (the management API accepts any int32)
classification_rationale: erlang:send_after/3 raised badarg inside the router and the gen_server terminate report printed the CommandRequest including plugin parameters. The reviewer's native label was MEDIUM; the derivation (I1, security control failed) is HIGH, so BLOCKING. send_after on the multiplied timeout exists on origin/dev
summary: Fixed in 91b2971b6: the timeout is clamped to 1..3600 seconds (a missing or non-positive one takes default_command_timeout_s), the router gets a counts-only format_status and joins the processes the crash filter protects, and a router that is down answers UNAVAILABLE. Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: one enrolled connection holding many pending sessions (Register without Subscribe) that each send a large fleet snapshot while the upstream is not draining
classification_rationale: buffer eviction is global and oldest first, so one connection pushed other agents' snapshots out; there was no per-connection bound. Native MEDIUM, derived HIGH. Pre-existing: the registry never bounded sessions per connection on origin/dev
summary: Fixed in 2818c7e48: max_sessions_per_connection (default 8, valid 1..1000) is applied where sessions are stored and asked before Register proxies upstream; refusals answer UNAVAILABLE and are counted in yuzu_gw_session_limit_rejected_total. Eviction stays global oldest first (see the open follow-up on fairness). Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: a reader of the BatchHeartbeat handler comment, or a heartbeat buffer crash that prints fleet tags
classification_rationale: grouped LOW items: the server handler comment did not state the drop contract for RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and INVALID_ARGUMENT (F3, comment only), and a buffer crash printed fleet status tags from the mailbox and stacktrace arguments (F4; fleet telemetry rather than credentials)
summary: Fixed in 73c32093e (the handler comment in the server states that those two codes must not be used for a transient capacity condition) and 7e884f2b6 (the buffer joins the processes yuzu_gw_crash_redact protects).

trigger: the command router process is down when a management SendCommand arrives
classification_rationale: the failure was answered INTERNAL and logged without naming the cause
summary: Fixed in 91b2971b6 (nearest commit; it carries the router_unavailable UNAVAILABLE answer and the rate limited WARN naming only the exit class).

trigger: one agent id repeating Register without Subscribe, or one connection sending 150 Registers with 3.5 MB hostnames
classification_rationale: the session cap counted distinct agent ids and pending rows were never superseded, so the advertised control was not enforced (I6 case a, false assurance): 40 Registers accepted with a cap of 8, and 150 x 3.5 MB held 510 MiB. Verified independently by gateway-erlang and security-guardian
summary: Fixed in c5541ce08: the cap counts rows, a Register of one agent id supersedes that agent's older pending rows, and reserve_session/2 checks and claims the slot atomically before the registration is proxied. Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: many concurrent Registers on one connection (200 sent)
classification_rationale: the check and the insert were separate steps so concurrent Registers all passed: 121 of 200 were proxied upstream and 113 orphan server sessions were left
summary: Fixed in c5541ce08 (atomic reservation) with the follow-on c627fd32d, which drops an uncommitted pending row without raising when the registry is gone (a related hardening of the same path, not a separately reported finding). Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: a heartbeat carrying about 3 MiB of invalid UTF-8 in its status tags, repeated by an agent
classification_rationale: repairing the tags cost the single buffer process 24 ms per heartbeat before the size bound was applied
summary: Fixed in b3519c658: the tag byte total is bounded before the repair runs, and the size is re-checked after it (a repair turns each invalid byte into three). Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: default_command_timeout_s is set to an invalid value in the gateway configuration
classification_rationale: the router logged an unthrottled WARN on every command for an invalid value
summary: Fixed in e3cf6b38a: the router warns at most once a minute and uses the default in between.

trigger: two overlapping Registers of one agent id on one connection, or a registry restart between the insert and the commit
classification_rationale: each commit removed the other's row and both answered ok, leaving zero pending rows, so both Subscribes got NOT_FOUND and the agent registered again
summary: Fixed in ec3244890: a commit answers an error when its own row is gone and changes nothing, and the supersede removes only the agent's rows stored at or before the committing row; tests cover every commit order and 200 rounds of 2 and 20 concurrent Registers. Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: a client that reconnects over and over after Register without Subscribe (3.5 MB hostnames)
classification_rationale: pending rows of a closed connection were kept until the TTL, so each reconnect started below the cap again: 184 MiB held after 25 s of churn and about 1.3 GB at steady state. Unbounded growth, I5. Pre-existing on dev (no connection-down handling existed)
summary: Fixed in cde787c23 (monitor the connection, remove its rows when it goes down), then refined in 71ee2b02f and f4a9ce791 to a grace. Decision recorded: dropping the rows at once broke the pinned GOAWAY behaviour, because a pending session must stay takeable by a Subscribe on the reconnected channel and released agents (v0.13.0 and rc6) wedge on NOT_FOUND (#2182). The owner session chose dead_connection_grace_ms (default 15 s, 0 to 120 s, 0 = at once) over an immediate drop; fd3e72287 pinned the interim behaviour and f4a9ce791 pins the grace. Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: a large pending table (10k to 40k rows from other connections) while one connection reserves or commits a session
classification_rationale: reserve, commit and the live insert counted a connection's rows by scanning the whole pending table inside the single registry process: a round trip cost 1 us to 41 ms at 10k rows and 184 ms at 40k
summary: Fixed in 7726ba0a9: a per-connection index written by the registry process only; the same index serves the supersede and the connection-down removal. fd3e72287 is the related test update. Verified by a scratch or real-application probe against a fake upstream, not a rig run.

trigger: an enrolled agent sends maximum-size invalid UTF-8 tags on every heartbeat
classification_rationale: informational: buffer CPU per attacker byte under repair. The cost is bounded by the tag byte bound added in b3519c658, so no further change was made. Recorded rejected because the closed disposition set has no accepted value; this is an accepted residual, not a disproved claim
summary: Accepted residual: the per-heartbeat repair work is bounded by the tag byte bound.

trigger: a stock gateway handling an agent registration wave (1000 agents, each ProxyRegister through the single upstream process)
classification_rationale: not a review finding: an unexplained rig observation (40 same-id Registers trickling at 2 per second) was traced to the probe client (a 500 ms coalesce window in the Erlang HTTP/2 client), and behind it to a real gateway limit. Nagle plus delayed ACK on the gateway-to-server socket made each ProxyRegister about 43 ms, about 24 per second per gateway: a stock gateway registered 703 of 1000 agents inside the agents' 30 s deadline and 2000 agents took 776 s. Derived MEDIUM (I5, recovery at fleet scale); pre-existing
summary: Fixed in 2e22932f4 (TCP_NODELAY on the upstream channel, application env upstream_tcp_nodelay, default true) with the pinning tests in c518edd93 and the docs in 3f03a1074. Evidence record: docs/security-reviews/gateway-heartbeat-verdict-replay-2026-10-04.md. Measured on the rig, see the pass 10 evidence row for the post-fix numbers.

trigger: a registration wave larger than the single upstream gen_server can serve inside the agent's 30 s deadline (after the nodelay fix the rate is about 1 ms per call)
classification_rationale: the nodelay fix removes the dominant cost but the registration RPC still runs inside the one upstream gen_server, requests whose caller has already given up are still served, and the upstream call deadline is not below the agent's 30 s
summary: Follow-up, the owner files an issue: run the proxy RPC outside the upstream gen_server, shed requests whose caller is gone, and set an upstream call deadline below the agent's 30 s. Reported NICE to SHOULD; derived I8 because the rate measured after the fix (K3 in the pass 10 evidence row) leaves headroom.

trigger: a Register that loses to a newer one, a dead connection among many rows, and the grace tests on a loaded shared CI box
classification_rationale: grouped LOW items: a superseded Register was answered registry_unavailable (a WARN and INTERNAL while the registry was healthy); drop_connection_rows scanned the whole table once per dead connection (about 0.87 ms per call over 20000 rows); the wall-clock margins of the grace tests could flake
summary: Fixed in 4af1e03f3 (a superseded Register is answered superseded, logged at INFO and answered UNAVAILABLE, the retryable class), bbf64cd94 (drop by the connection index, not a scan) and 9e777e755 (the grace tests deliver the timer's own message instead of relying on elapsed time). security-guardian reported no findings in this round.

trigger: a hot code load of yuzu_gw_registry or yuzu_gw_upstream with changed state records
classification_rationale: INFO: code_change/3 is the identity with no relup. Accepted: no live upgrade path exists (deployment is restart), the same position as the round 3 appup row. Recorded rejected because the closed disposition set has no accepted value
summary: Not changed; see R3-g8b3-appup-relup-stale for the rationale.

trigger: a stock gateway configuration under registration waves, outages and restarts (rig pass 6 on c518edd93)
classification_rationale: the docs described rig pass 6 as pending; this row records its results. K0 nodelay verified on the stock config. K1 1000 agents registered in 1.89 to 2.11 s with 0 deadline failures (3 runs); K2 2000 agents 4.16 s; K3 5000 agents 12.08 s; the control with upstream_tcp_nodelay=false reproduced 297 deadline failures of 1000 (last agent 55.5 s). K4 recovery with real agents: 30 agents after a 12 s outage 15.5 s; 45 agents after 150 s 17.3 s with 0 drops; 1 agent after 300 s 0.98 s (an open-breaker variant 52.9 s); three gateway kills with 20 agents: 20 of 20 each round, 0 refused. K5 grace: a Subscribe within 1 s is served, rows are 0 at 17 s, refused at 20 s. K6 server restart with 1000 agents: all back in 22.7 to 23.3 s for 10 s and 60 s outages, 2000 agents 46.1 s, recovery linear at about 22.5 ms per agent (the 20 ms replay spacing); notify_dropped at_capacity 987 after a 1000 agent cold Subscribe wave (MAX_NOTIFY_INFLIGHT 10, pre-existing; route rows stay tombstoned until the replay, the existing dropped-notify row). K7 five minutes of steady state clean
summary: Not covered by that build: the last four code commits (4af1e03f3, bbf64cd94, 9e777e755, 4ddeac911), which were verified by eunit 650 of 650, dialyzer, Common Test 52 and mutants. Not run: the 5000 agent stock run with nodelay off, and K6 at 5000 agents (an extrapolated 115 s, not measured).

trigger: a Subscribe the gateway refuses (for example NOT_FOUND for an unknown session), which throws {grpc_error, {NOT_FOUND, ...}} from yuzu_gw_agent_service:subscribe/2 inside a streaming handler
classification_rationale: the throw crashes the grpcbox bidirectional stream process (an error level crasher log) and reaches the client as status 2 (process exited without reason) instead of NOT_FOUND (5). The same throw pattern is on origin/dev. The C++ agent re-registers on any non-OK status, so no functional effect was observed
summary: Follow-up, the owner decides: return the grpc error instead of throwing in streaming handlers. Observed on the rig during pass 6.

trigger: an agent whose fleet snapshot table grows to about 2 MiB
classification_rationale: the agent proto promises a snapshot of 5 to 20 KB but the table can reach 2 MiB; the gateway bounds what it keeps but the agent has no byte budget of its own. Raised across the later review rounds
summary: Follow-up, the owner files an issue: add an agent-side snapshot byte budget.

trigger: any BatchHeartbeat or Register larger than the default server receive limit
classification_rationale: the server relies on the gRPC default 4194304 byte receive limit, which the gateway chunking is designed around but nothing sets explicitly. Raised across the later review rounds
summary: Follow-up, the owner files an issue: set the maximum receive message size explicitly on the server so the limit the gateway chunks against cannot drift.

trigger: one connection at its session cap sending large snapshots while the upstream is not draining
classification_rationale: per-connection fairness of the buffer is bounded by max_sessions_per_connection, but eviction is still global and oldest first, so one connection can still displace others within its cap. The residual of R5-sec-f2-one-connection-evicts-others
summary: Follow-up, the owner files an issue: evict per connection before global oldest first.
